correctness.rationale: The structural induction fixes term outputs in {0,1,x,1−x}, with comparisons constant on five strata. Constructed crisp characteristic terms partition these strata and independently realize any admissible four-choice output per stratum. Distinctness at 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1 gives 192 and injective five-point restriction. The same argument counts finite n and proves odd n≥5 exactly; midpoint/strict-left separators cover every excluded n. In-package standard-library verifier exactly enumerated the full unary closure and independently generated piecewise normal forms for n=2..17; only the proof handles infinitely many n and the continuum. No numerical approximation was used in the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Earlier Gödel involution theory supplies the connectives, Baaz Delta and characteristic values, but not the specific simultaneous canonical classification over the continuum and all equally spaced finite chains. Its observation that individual truth degrees cannot always be characterized for larger chains is about definability of constants, not equality of arbitrary unary terms; thus it does not contradict or imply the odd-size equational completeness test by itself. The new claim is not a direct instance of the modal complexity theorems, the ordinary Gödel-free-algebra dualities, or the Chang-chain free-algebra product. Residual risk: a functional-clone normal-form theorem under another name might imply it.

value.rationale: Determines a complete and naturally motivated one-generated term-function algebra rather than an arbitrary low-dimensional slice. The exact five-point test reduces all unary continuum equations to five concrete evaluations, and parity sharpness shows every large even chain still fails to detect the midpoint characteristic identity. The distinction from older point-definability work is mathematically useful for formula equality, algebraic simplification and single-variable semantic testing in the nonmodal reduct; no unsupported extension to modal or multivariable logics is claimed.
